normalized.governing_thought: Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a per-seat Pro plan: it is the only option that lifts NRR toward 105% and keeps gross margin above 75%
executive_summary: Recommendation: launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a new Pro plan at +$12 per seat per month ($91 vs $79 Core) with a pooled AI-usage allowance. Do not launch it as a $149 per-account add-on, and make the mobile app rewrite the next engineering priority. Plan on $1.7–2.9M of expansion ARR (+3.0–5.0 NRR points), not the $8M in the proposal.
Launch: a paid Copilot is needed to reach the NRR target, and the beta shows real value
Reaching 105% NRR takes +4 points, about $2.3M of net expansion a year. Removing every mobile-related churn would add only 3.8 points
In the beta, jobs per dispatcher-hour rose 11% against 2% for matched accounts. The gain is real, but volunteer bias inflates it
Routewise now includes AI in its Pro plan. AI explains at most ~$0.6M a year of lost new ARR, a third of Sales’ $1.9M estimate
Packaging and price: a per-seat Pro plan beats the $149 add-on, a free bundle and not launching
Purchases point to 7–14% buying the add-on, not the 46% who said they would: ~$1.2–2.5M ARR, mostly from the heaviest users
Pro at +$12 per seat costs every account 15% more. If 20–33% of accounts move to it: $1.7–2.9M ARR and +3.0–5.0 NRR points
Giving Copilot free in Core cuts company gross margin to 72–74%, below the 75% floor
Trade-offs: accept the two-quarter mobile delay on purpose, protect margin, and launch in stages
The mobile delay loses ~$0.3–0.8M ARR to churn that could have been avoided. Launching Copilot first still reaches 105% about two quarters sooner
An allowance of 500 requests per seat caps AI cost at $4.50 per $12 seat. Company gross margin stays at 76% or more
Test on non-volunteer accounts in Q1 and check results at end of Q3 (go-ahead if ≥13% have moved to Pro). The 14 Copilot engineers move to mobile in Q3 2027

slides.title: We tested the CPO’s $149 add-on plan against five conditions. Two failed, so we kept the launch but changed the packaging

claims.claim: Starting hypothesis: launch Copilot in Q2 2027 as a paid add-on at $149 per account per month, worth ~$8M of ARR in year 1
A. About 46% of accounts buy at $149 (≈$8M ARR): NOT SUPPORTED: $1.2–2.5M is realistic
evidence: The survey reached only 6% of admins, and respondents run larger accounts (9.4 seats vs 6.2)
In the paywall test, 14% of beta volunteers actually paid

claims.claim: B. A flat price per account pays off at every level of usage: NOT SUPPORTED: heavy users self-select
evidence: Add-on buyers average 6,800 requests a month ($61 of AI cost)
The top 10% average 14,500 ($131), against a $149 price

claims.claim: C. Copilot creates real value for customers: SUPPORTED: size uncertain
evidence: Jobs per dispatcher-hour +11% vs +2% for matched accounts
4.1 hours a week saved (self-reported); all from volunteers

claims.claim: D. Copilot is needed to hit 105% NRR and to compete: SUPPORTED for NRR; competitive effect limited
evidence: Fixing mobile adds at most 3.8 NRR points
Routewise includes AI in Pro, and our win rate fell from 44% to 37%

claims.claim: E. We can afford to delay mobile by two quarters: PARTLY: only if mobile is next and Customer Success limits the damage
evidence: Mobile is the top churn reason (27%) and the top feature request (38%)
A 6-month delay costs ~$0.3–0.8M ARR

claims.claim: Revised answer: Launch in Q2 2027: yes (C, D hold; E holds with conditions). Packaging: change from a $149 per-account add-on to a per-seat Pro plan with a usage allowance (A and B fail).

slides.title: Reaching 105% NRR takes ~$2.3M of net expansion a year. Retention fixes alone cannot get there, so Copilot has to be paid for

claims.claim: Reaching 105% NRR takes ~$2.3M of net expansion a year
evidence: Target: 101% → 105% NRR = +4 pts × $57.6M = $2.30M a year

claims.claim: Mobile ceiling: even fixing 100% of mobile-related churn adds only 3.8 points
evidence: ARR lost to churn: 14% logo churn × $57.6M ≈ $8.06M a year
Mobile-related: 27% × $8.06M = $2.18M = 3.8 pts maximum
AI-related: 6% × $8.06M = $0.48M = 0.8 pts maximum

claims.claim: NRR points each option could add, low to high case
evidence: Needed: +4.0
Pro plan, +$12/seat (20–33% of accounts move): 3.0–5.0
$149 add-on (7–14% of accounts buy): 2.1–4.3
Mobile rewrite (prevents 25–75% of mobile churn): 0.9–2.8
Stop all AI-related churn (0–100%): 0.0–0.8
Pro: accounts moving × 6.2 seats × $12 × 12 months. 33% → $2.89M (+5.0); 20% → $1.75M (+3.0)

claims.claim: Accounts needed to reach the target alone: Pro 26%; add-on 13%, which is about the beta volunteers’ own buying rate
Moving accounts to Pro is a one-off jump, while the mobile fix keeps paying every year. We need both.

slides.title: The beta shows a real productivity gain, but the volunteers were larger and more active than typical accounts, so plan on less than the headline

claims.claim: The beta shows a real productivity gain
evidence: Change in jobs scheduled per dispatcher-hour vs the prior 12 weeks: Beta accounts +11%; Matched non-beta +2%
+9 pts net gain vs matched accounts

claims.claim: Why we discount it
evidence: Volunteers: beta accounts average 8.1 seats (vs 6.2) and are more active than the base
Self-reported: the 4.1 hours a week saved is not measured
Concentrated: the top 10% of accounts made 58% of AI requests

claims.claim: The value is clear even after a heavy discount
evidence: At half the hours saved (~8.9 a month), Pro costs an average account ~$8 per dispatcher-hour saved ($4 at the full figure)
$/hour = Pro uplift for an average account ($74.40 a month) ÷ dispatcher hours saved a month (4.1 × 52 ÷ 12 = 17.8)

claims.claim: Do not assume the full gain in pricing or forecasts. Measure it in non-volunteer accounts in the Q1 test before launch
90-day renewal points the right way, but the window is short and the accounts chose to take part
evidence: 90-day renewal: 97% for beta accounts vs 93% for matched accounts
240 volunteer accounts, 12 weeks

slides.title: Routewise has made AI a must-have, but AI explains at most ~$0.6M a year of lost new ARR, a third of the Sales estimate

claims.claim: AI explains at most ~$0.6M a year of lost new ARR
evidence: Routewise competes in 60% × 2,600 = 1,560 deals a year
Upper limit: AI caused the whole 7-pt drop in win rate: $0.64M
If half the drop came from Routewise’s price cut: $0.32M
New account = 6.2 seats × $79 × 12 = $5,878 ARR

claims.claim: Why the Sales memo overstates it
evidence: Sales memo: 63% of deals lost × 1,560 = 983 lost; a third of them = 328 deals × $5,878 = $1.93M
Mentioning AI in a loss note (31%) does not show AI caused the loss, and we were already losing 56% of these deals before Routewise had AI
Routewise also offered 20% off the first year in Q3 2026, the same quarter the win rate fell

claims.claim: Copilot in Pro is needed to defend against Routewise’s Pro plan, but the case must not count more than ~$0.6M of new ARR from it
evidence: New-customer ARR does not count toward NRR

slides.title: The $8M add-on forecast relies on what a small, skewed sample said it would do. Actual purchases point to ~$1.9M of ARR and ~$0.5M of gross profit

claims.claim: Why the survey misleads
evidence: 6% response: 610 of 9,800 admins replied
Larger accounts: respondents average 9.4 seats vs 6.2 overall
Intent, not purchase: "likely to buy" is not buying

claims.claim: Why 14% is the most it could be
evidence: In the paywall test, 17 of 120 beta accounts paid after 12 free weeks
Beta accounts are volunteers, larger and more active, so the full base is likely to buy at a lower rate. Low case 7% → $1.2M ARR

claims.claim: $149 add-on, year 1 bridge ($M)
evidence: Survey intent → paywall purchases 46% → 14%: −$5.61M
Paywall purchase rate: $2.45M
Adjust for larger beta accounts 14% → 10.7%: −$0.58M
Expected add-on ARR: $1.87M
Platform, evaluation and support: −$0.60M
Gross profit: $0.51M

claims.claim: The add-on’s gross margin is thin (~27%), because buyers are heavy users

slides.title: A flat $149 fee attracts the heaviest users and raises an average account’s bill by 30%. A per-seat price keeps price in line with use

claims.claim: AI cost per account per month vs the $149 price
evidence: Median beta account: 1,900 requests, $17
Mean beta account: 3,600 requests, $32
Add-on buyers: 6,800 requests, $61
Top 10% of accounts: 14,500 requests, $130
AI cost = requests × $0.009 (contract price, fixed to December 2027)

claims.claim: People who buy a flat fee use far more than average: buyers make 1.9× the mean number of requests, and the top 10% leave only ~$18 a month of margin
A fee per account hits small contractors hardest: +63% for a 3-seat account vs +4% at 50 seats
evidence: 3 seats: Core $237/mo; $149 add-on +63%; Pro +$36 (+15%)

claims.claim: Price already drives churn: it is the main reason for 22% of churn, second only to mobile
Per seat charges every account the same 15% and grows with the number of dispatchers using Copilot

slides.title: A pooled allowance of 500 AI requests per Pro seat keeps company gross margin at 76% or more, even if heavy users all move to Pro

claims.claim: Company gross margin by option (%), 75% floor
evidence: Today (Core only): 78.0%
Pro with allowance, 20% move: 76.5%
Pro with allowance, 33% move: 76.3%
Pro, no allowance, heavy use: 74.1%
Free in Core, 50% use it: 74.4%
Free in Core, all use it: 71.9%

claims.claim: How the allowance protects margin
evidence: Cap: 500 requests × $0.009 = $4.50 of AI cost per $12 seat, so at least 62% of the uplift is kept before platform cost
Pooled across the account: an average 6.2-seat account gets 3,100 requests, more than the median beta account uses (1,900)
Heavy users pay: packs of 10,000 requests at $200 a month ($0.02 per request, 55% margin)

claims.claim: Without it: if Pro accounts use as much as add-on buyers, margin falls to 74.1%, below the floor
evidence: "Heavy use" assumes Pro accounts use as much as add-on buyers (6,800 requests a month)

claims.claim: Possible gain from 2028: if the provider’s 35% fall in list prices carries through, cost per request falls to $0.0059 and margin rises to ~76.9%
evidence: our price is fixed to December 2027

slides.title: The recommended offer: Copilot only in Pro at +$12 per seat, with pooled usage, paid packs for heavy users and a 30-day trial

claims.claim: Plan structure: Core stays at $79 per seat with no change. New Pro at $91 per seat per month includes all three Copilot features: schedule proposals, quote drafts and call summaries
evidence: Matches how Routewise packages AI (inside Pro). Existing Core customers see no price change

claims.claim: Price point: +$12 per seat per month (+15%)
evidence: Price proposed in the pack, backed by the 2023 tier launch (33% moved). ~$4–8 per dispatcher-hour saved

claims.claim: Heavy users: Packs of 10,000 requests for $200 a month

claims.claim: Trial: 30-day Pro trial inside the product for Core accounts
evidence: In the paywall test, buying followed use

claims.claim: Beta accounts: Move all 240 to Pro at launch. The 17 who already pay for the add-on switch at a lower price
evidence: $97 vs $149 at 8.1 seats

claims.claim: New customers: Pro is the default quote in deals where Routewise competes
Price review: Review price, allowance and pack size after two quarters of data

slides.title: Launching Copilot first costs ~$0.3–0.8M of ARR to mobile churn. On ARR it is a close call, but it is the only order that reaches 105% NRR by H1 2028

claims.claim: Copilot first (recommended) vs Mobile first
evidence: Permanent ARR lost: Copilot first ~$0.27–0.82M to mobile churn (25–75% of $2.18M a year × 0.5 years); Mobile first up to ~$0.56M: ≤$0.32M of new ARR to Routewise + ≤$0.24M of AI-related churn (upper limits)
Pro revenue timing: Copilot first builds from Q2 2027 to $1.7–2.9M ARR by Q2 2028; Mobile first $0.9–1.4M of Pro revenue arrives later
Mobile rewrite: Copilot first lands two quarters later, the 14 engineers join it in Q3 2027; Mobile first lands two quarters sooner
When NRR can reach 105%: Copilot first H1 2028; Mobile first late 2028 at best, likely to slip
Engineering cost: $1.47M (14 × 0.5 years × $210k); Mobile first the same $1.47M, two quarters later

claims.claim: How to limit the mobile cost
evidence: Customer Success outreach: contact accounts that have raised mobile complaints, the 27% churn group
Publish a dated mobile roadmap
Copilot’s 14 engineers move to mobile in Q3 2027 after launch; no follow-on AI features ahead of mobile
Keep the launch to the three beta features
Track mobile-related churn monthly; if it rises above the 2026 rate, raise it at the Q3 review

claims.claim: On permanent ARR this is a close call, and doing mobile first may lose slightly less. What decides it is timing: only Copilot first gives Pro time to deliver its uplift before the 2028 NRR target, while Routewise’s AI is still new. The mobile fix then keeps NRR up once the one-off Pro gain is used up.

slides.title: Appendix A: every figure in the deck comes from the briefing pack using the calculations below

claims.claim: Calculations behind the deck's figures
evidence: Current ARR: 9,800 accounts × 6.2 seats × $79 × 12 = $57.6M
Today’s gross profit / cost of revenue: 78% × $57.6M / 22% × $57.6M = $44.9M / $12.7M
NRR target gap: (105% − 101%) × $57.6M = $2.30M a year
Add-on AI cost: Buyers × 6,800 requests × $0.009 × 12 = $1.01M at 14%; $0.77M at 10.7%
Pro AI cost at full allowance: Accounts × 3,100 requests × $0.009 × 12 = $1.08M at 33%; $0.66M at 20%
Free in Core AI cost: Accounts × 2,756 requests (444 per seat × 6.2) × $0.009 × 12 = $2.92M (all) / $1.46M (50%)
Win-rate gap: 2,600 × 60% × 7 pts × $5,878 = $0.64M new ARR a year
Copilot engineering: 14 × 0.5 years × $210,000 = $1.47M
Company gross margin: ($44.9M + new revenue − AI cost − $0.6M) ÷ ($57.6M + new revenue); e.g. Pro 33%: $46.1M ÷ $60.5M = 76.3%
Mobile delay cost: $2.18M × 25–75% prevented × 0.5 years = $0.27–0.82M ARR
Pro vs add-on break-even: $1.87M ÷ (9,800 × 6.2 × $144) = 21% of accounts

normalized.recommendation: Launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a new Pro plan at +$12 per seat per month ($91 vs $79 Core) with a pooled AI-usage allowance. Do not launch it as a $149 per-account add-on, and make the mobile app rewrite the next engineering priority. Plan on $1.7–2.9M of expansion ARR (+3.0–5.0 NRR points), not the $8M in the proposal. Decisions requested: approve the Q2 2027 Pro launch at $91/seat; drop the $149 add-on and free-in-Core option; assign 14 engineers to Copilot for Q1–Q2 2027 and accept the two-quarter mobile delay, with engineers moving to mobile in Q3 2027; adopt the 500-requests-per-seat allowance, $200 packs of 10,000 requests and a 76% gross-margin guardrail; order the Q1 test with non-volunteer accounts and the three reviews, and reset the plan to $1.7–2.9M of expansion ARR.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Tested as the starting hypothesis; conditions A and B not supported. Realistic $1.2–2.5M ARR (7–14% buy), ~$1.87M central, ~$0.5M gross profit, thin ~27% margin, attracts heaviest users, +30% price rise for average account (+63% at 3 seats). Verdict: Second best; drop it.
Cuts company gross margin to 71.9–74.4%, below the 75% floor; negative gross profit; NRR ≤0.8. Verdict: Breaks margin floor; drop it. Do not fall back to it if Q3 review is missed.

$0 expansion ARR; mobile fix adds 0.9–2.8 NRR points later; GM 78.0%. Verdict: Misses NRR target. On permanent ARR a close call and may lose slightly less (up to ~$0.56M), but NRR 105% only late 2028 at best, likely to slip.

alternatives_considered.option: Pro plan, +$12 per seat with pooled allowance
alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommended: $1.7–2.9M ARR, +3.0 to +5.0 NRR points, GM 76.3–76.5%, matches Routewise, +15% for every size.

alternatives_considered.option: Copilot first vs mobile first sequencing
alternatives_considered.treatment: Copilot first recommended: costs ~$0.27–0.82M to mobile churn, but is the only order that reaches 105% NRR by H1 2028.
If Pro accounts use as much as add-on buyers, margin falls to 74.1%, below the floor; allowance adopted.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: The pack states all figures are synthetic benchmark data
Assumes accounts that move to Pro or churn are average size (6.2 seats)
Mobile-fix share (25–75%, central 50%) is our assumption; the pack has no estimate
Beta results come from volunteers (8.1 seats vs 6.2, more active); hours saved (4.1/week) are self-reported; 90-day renewal window is short — treated as upper limits
Adjusting for beta size scales 14% by 6.2 ÷ 8.1 seats (our assumption) → 10.7% central; 7% low
Platform cost ($0.6M a year) counted as cost of revenue; year-1 figures at full run rate
Pro AI cost at the full allowance (3,100 requests per average account)
Assumes doing mobile first delays Copilot by the same two quarters (same engineering capacity)
AI cost $0.009 per request fixed to December 2027; a rise in 2028 would cut margin; a 35% fall in list prices could raise margin to ~76.9%
Share of accounts moving to Pro is the key sensitivity: below 26% Pro alone misses +4 NRR pts; below ~21% Pro brings less ARR than the add-on central case
Win-rate drop counted as up to 100% AI only as an upper limit; Routewise also offered 20% off in Q3 2026
Allowance, pack price, trial and review thresholds are design choices to confirm in the Q1 test
Likelihood and impact of risks are our judgement; owners are proposals for the executive team to confirm
Data gaps: top-10% usage share (40% computed vs 58% stated) doesn't agree; churn counts (1,190 vs 1,372 implied) don't match; survey sample skewed (6% response, 9.4 seats)

Six risks: fewer accounts move to Pro (<26%); heavy AI usage erodes margin; mobile churn rises during delay; productivity gain does not repeat outside volunteers; Routewise wins on price not AI; AI cost per request rises after 2027
next_steps: Q1 2027: build, harden and test with ~500 randomly chosen non-volunteer Core accounts; end-of-Q1 go/no-go (≥8% take Pro within 6 weeks; jobs per dispatcher-hour ≥+5% vs control; usage within allowance for ≥85% of accounts)
Q2 2027: Pro launch; 30-day trial; move all 240 beta accounts to Pro
Customer Success outreach to accounts with mobile complaints; publish dated mobile roadmap
Q3 2027: 14 Copilot engineers move to mobile rewrite; renegotiate the 2028 AI contract by Q3 2027
End of Q3 2027 review: Pro migration ≥13%; company GM ≥76%; mobile-related churn no higher than the 2026 rate; if missed, reprice or widen the trial
Review price, allowance and pack size after two quarters of data
Q2 2028 outcome check: Pro ≥26% of accounts; trailing-12-month NRR ≥104%, heading for 105%; mobile rewrite on its dated plan
Product to reconcile the conflicting usage figures
